success.description: Disputed source-derived lower bound for complete six-round AES-128 key recovery under the author model. Section6 explicitly claims >95% for selecting the correct first32-bit diagonal at2^72.77 chosen plaintexts, then completes the remaining96 bits by exhaustive search at the same configuration total2^104.92+2^96 approximately2^104.93 six-round encryptions. Under that stated finalization, correct-diagonal recovery suffices for full-key recovery, so the source-model bound propagates without four independent95% factors. The source does not separately print a whole-key percentage. This inference inherits the existing sampling-model arithmetic conflict; it is not an independently established or measured full-key guarantee.

review.scope: Verified extraction of the author stage claim and its same-budget complete96-bit finalization, independently checked against original Sections6/AppendixE and Algorithm2. Verified does not certify the disputed sampling model, key-search uniqueness, actual success distribution or attack correctness.

PDF21–22 claim >95% for finding the first diagonal at about 2^73.343 source sets / 2^72.77 chosen plaintexts. The existing Equation11/sample-count arithmetic conflict applies to this claim, so it remains a disputed component, not a certified whole-key rate.

PDF22: once the correct first 32-bit diagonal is known, complete enumeration of the remaining 96 key bits includes the true key. This conditional inclusion event neither validates the statistical first stage nor quantifies uniqueness at a truncated search budget.

limitations: The paper uses approximate probability, binomial/normal and wrong-key models. Reviewer arithmetic controls are not a proof of those independence assumptions.
20 table/S-box look-ups per AES round is the source comparison approximation; lookup-table sizes differ (PDF p.17 footnote10). Native units are not interchangeable with unrelated papers.
Unreported memory or preprocessing is unknown, not zero; no same-method Pareto conclusion follows from time/data alone.
